result.title: Curvature Mismatch and Local Errors in Galaxy Property Estimation
result.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026)
result.summary: Linear probes are widely used to evaluate learned representations and infer physical quantities from unlabelled data. The probe's predictions are from an affine function in ambient space restricted to the underlying representation, and consequently, even a representation that has complete information needed to predict a target can produce systematic probe errors when that information is encoded in a form inaccessible to the linear probe. Here we share that some of this probing error is due to the innate geometry of the manifold. Linear probes, when evaluated on a curved manifold, generally have a nonzero intrinsic Hessian (what we colloquially call "probe-facing curvature") given by $\langle w_N,\mathrm{II}\rangle$, the manifold's second fundamental form dotted with the probe's normal component. We fit linear probes to galaxy embeddings from five pretrained encoders and intervene on this curvature term to evaluate its contribution to the probe performance. We find that keeping this inherited curvature improves the local fit where it matches the label's curvature. Removing the curvature component of the probe where it does not match the label curvature also provides improvements, and correcting it in every neighbourhood raises held-out local $R^2$ by 0.006 to 0.010 on galaxies, gaining more where the two curvatures disagree. We isolated these gains to be from the underlying geometry and not an automatic guarantee from least squares training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在五个预训练编码器的星系嵌入上拟合线性探针，提出由流形第二基本形式与探针法向分量内积给出的「probe-facing curvature」，并通过干预该曲率项评估内在几何对探针误差的贡献，在星系属性估计上获得小幅局部 R² 提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察——信息虽在表示中但线性探针无法读取，部分误差来自表示流形的曲率——可为判断 VLM 内部状态是否真正保留视觉细节提供表示几何的诊断视角，曲率分解与干预能否用于 latent 状态分析可供核查。
